```{=html}
<div class="bear-home-heading"><div class="bear-home-title"><h1>BEAR</h1><p>Benchmarks of Empirical Accuracy in Research</p></div>
<div class="bear-home-logo"><img src="assets/bear_banner.png" alt="BEAR silhouette"></div></div>
<div class="proposal-row first-row">
<section class="proposal-box problem-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8"/><path d="M12 7v6m0 4h.01"/></svg><h2 id="problem">Problem</h2>
<p>Quantitative metascience drives important debates about research
standards. Most of its crucial contributions have been based on
analysing individual datasets, often painstakingly constructed by
researchers. Thanks to their work we now have a better understanding of
replicability, publication bias, p-hacking, reporting practices,
pre-registration, significance rates, and more. But many canonical
findings of metascience are based on individual datasets, each
constructed in a specific way. How generalisable are these findings?</p>
</section>
<section class="proposal-box solution-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="3" y="4" width="7" height="7" rx="1"/><rect x="14" y="13" width="7" height="7" rx="1"/><path d="M14 7h6v3M4 14v3h6"/></svg><h2 id="solution">Solution</h2>
<p>BEAR is an open-source database for exploring metascience with over
20 datasets across many scientific fields and millions of data points.
BEAR does not generate any new source data; it repackages publicly
available datasets into a common structure to make research on
replication, exchangeability, meta-analysis, and other questions about
empirical research easier and more generalisable.</p>
</section>
<section class="proposal-box download-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 3v12m-5-5 5 5 5-5M4 16v5h16v-5"/></svg><h2>How to download</h2>
<p>BEAR currently works best in R.</p>
<blockquote class="download-notice"><p>To download all data in one table,
<code>BEAR.rds</code>, go to <a href="https://github.com/wwiecek/BEAR/releases">GitHub Releases</a> page.</p></blockquote>
<p class="download-guide">You can download individual datasets (which can include
additional variables and rows), see <a href="datasets.html">Datasets</a> page.
See <a href="getting-started.html">Get data</a> for more details.</p>
<a class="box-button" href="https://github.com/wwiecek/BEAR/releases">GitHub Releases <span aria-hidden="true">&#8599;&#xfe0e;</span></a>
</section>
</div>
```

{{< include _site_metrics.md >}}

```{=html}
<div class="proposal-row second-row">
<section class="proposal-box datasets-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><ellipse cx="12" cy="5" rx="8" ry="3"/><path d="M4 5v7c0 4 16 4 16 0V5M4 12v7c0 4 16 4 16 0v-7"/></svg><h2 id="datasets">Datasets</h2>
<p>BEAR combines curated registries of studies (e.g. clinicaltrials.gov), 
random collections of articles in different disciplines, and sets of meta-analyses. 
These are purposefully heterogeneous sets of varying quality. 
The database covers many disciplines: economics,
political science, biomedicine, clinical trials, ecology, evolution,
education, neuroscience, and more.</p>
<a class="box-button" href="datasets.html">Datasets <span aria-hidden="true">&#8599;&#xfe0e;</span></a>
</section>
<section class="proposal-box uses-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 20V4m0 16h16M8 16l4-7 4 3 4-7"/></svg><h2 id="what-is-in-each-dataset">What is in each dataset?</h2>
<p>At a minimum BEAR contains z-values with clearly labelled identifiers
for studies and meta-analyses. Where available, it also includes effect
sizes, standard errors, sample sizes, methods (e.g. parallel RCT),
measures (e.g. standardised mean difference, odds ratio), and additional
covariates (e.g. year, pre-registration status, phase of the clinical
trial, journal, discipline).</p>
<a class="box-button" href="documentation.html">Documentation <span aria-hidden="true">&#8599;&#xfe0e;</span></a>
</section>
<section class="proposal-box model-box"><svg class="section-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 20V4m0 16h16M8 16l4-7 4 3 4-7"/></svg><h2 id="model">Model</h2>
<p>An optional model of signal-to-noise ratios is also
included as part of the repository, to quantify basic metascientific parameters
like selection, assurance, and replicability of findings. Users are encouraged
to fit their own models. We make use of that model in an upcoming paper,
"A Statistical Case For Qualified Scientific Optimism"
(van Zwet, Gelman, and Więcek 2026).</p>
<a class="box-button" href="https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/research/unpublished/A_statistical_case_for_qualified_scientific_optimism.pdf">Read the paper <span aria-hidden="true">&#8599;&#xfe0e;</span></a>
</section>
</div>
<section class="credits"><h2 id="credits">Credits</h2>
<p>All credit is due to the researchers who assembled the metascientific
datasets and maintain the large-scale repositories from which data are
compiled here. Please see individual dataset pages for references and
licensing information.</p>
</section>
```
